questions.title: Mathematical Terms, Scales, and Road Signs

subQuestions.questionText: Use TABLE 1 to choose an explanation or definition from COLUMN B that matches the term or concept in COLUMN A. Match: Circumference
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: E (the boundary that surrounds a circular shape)
Mark 1: 1A correct option
Full marks for written explanations also accepted.

subQuestions.questionText: Match: Probability
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: G (the likelihood that something might happen)
Mark 1: 1A correct option

subQuestions.questionText: Match: One hour
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: F (a time measurement equivalent to three thousand six hundred seconds)
Mark 1: 1A correct option

subQuestions.questionText: Match: Temperature
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (the measuring of hotness or coldness)
Mark 1: 1A correct option

subQuestions.questionText: Three sketches represent the same portion of the physical world drawn using three different scales (A: 1:100 000, B: 1:25 000, C: 1:50 000) in random order. Name the type of scale used to draw the sketches.
subQuestions.memoText:
Numerical / Number / Ratio / Number-ratio scale.
Mark 1-2: 2A type of scale (2 marks)
subQuestions.topic: Maps, Plans and Other Representations - Scale

subQuestions.questionText: Interpret the scale 1 : 50 000.
subQuestions.memoText:
1 unit on the map is equivalent to 50 000 units in real life.
OR: The map is 50 000 times smaller than real life.
Mark 1-2: 2A relationship (2 marks)
subQuestions.topic: Maps, Plans and Other Representations - Scale

subQuestions.questionText: Write down the scale that was used to draw Sketch 2.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: 1 : 25 000
Mark 1-2: 2A correct scale (Accept B) (2 marks)
subQuestions.topic: Maps, Plans and Other Representations - Scale

subQuestions.questionText: Give the shapes of the information boards. (Refer to picture of information boards in the question paper showing a traffic sign and distance information sign.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Rectangle and a circle.
Mark 1: 1A rectangle
Mark 2: 1A circle
Accept 'round' for circle.
subQuestions.topic: Maps, Plans and Other Representations - Shapes

subQuestions.questionText: Write down the distance a motorist must still travel, in a northerly direction, to reach Bloemfontein.
subQuestions.memoText:
144 km
Mark 1-2: 2A correct answer (Accept 144) (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: The 120 on the traffic sign board indicates 120 km/h. Interpret 120 km/h in context.
subQuestions.memoText:
It is the maximum speed a motorist can travel on the road.
OR: The motorist can cover a distance of 120 km in 1 hour.
OR: 120 km/h is the speed limit / Do not exceed 120 km/h on this road.
Mark 1-2: 2A correct explanation (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the distance from Trompsburg to Johannesburg. (Trompsburg is 27 km away, Johannesburg is 534 km away from the information board.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Distance (Jhb - Trompsburg) = 534 - 27 = 507 km
Mark 1: 1RT both correct values (534 and 27)
Mark 2: 1A distance (507 km)
NPU (no penalty for omitting unit)
Note: For candidates writing 534 - 144 = 390, award 1 out of 2.

subQuestions.questionText: State the general direction of Trompsburg from the information sign.
subQuestions.memoText:
North / N
Mark 1-2: 2A correct direction (2 marks)
subQuestions.topic: Maps, Plans and Other Representations - Directions

subQuestions.questionText: The length of one of the road signs is 90 cm. Convert this length to metres.
subQuestions.memoText:
$\frac{90 \text{ cm}}{100} = 0,9$ m
Mark 1: 1MA dividing by 100
Mark 2: 1A simplification (0,9 m)

questions.title: Bloem Agricultural Show, Pedal Go-Karts, and Probability

subQuestions.questionText: Use ANNEXURE A (site map of the Bloem Agricultural Show). Write down the gate number for the main public entrance.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: 2
Mark 1-2: 2A correct number (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: State the maximum number of public parking areas available.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: 6
Mark 1-2: 2A correct road (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the number of gates used by vehicles.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: 7
Mark 1-2: 2A correct number (2 marks)
Note: Listing all seven correct (1, 5, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12) - Vehicle entrance, cattle vehicle, etc. - award 1 out of 2.

subQuestions.questionText: Write down only the letter that makes the following statement TRUE: The probability of finding a gate on the eastern side of the site is ...
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (certain)
Mark 1-2: 2A correct choice (2 marks)
Accept Certain.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the general direction of Gate 12 from the Amusement Park.
subQuestions.memoText:
South East (SE)
Mark 1-2: 2A correct direction (2 marks)
subQuestions.topic: Maps, Plans and Other Representations - Directions

subQuestions.questionText: A layout plan will be drawn of this site map using a scale of 1 : 8 000. The Daisy Hall has a length of 65 m. Determine, rounded to the nearest mm, the length of the Daisy Hall on this layout plan.
subQuestions.memoText:
Length = 65 m = 65 000 mm
Scale: 1 : 8 000, so n : 65 000
$n = \frac{65\,000}{8\,000} = 8,125$ mm $\approx 8$ mm
Mark 1: 1C conversion (m to mm)
Mark 2: 1MA dividing
Mark 3: 1CA simplification (8,125 mm)
Mark 4: 1R rounding (≈ 8 mm)
Alternative method:
Scale 1:8000, n:65, $n = \frac{65}{8000} = 0,008125$ m = 8,125 mm ≈ 8 mm
subQuestions.topic: Maps, Plans and Other Representations - Scale

subQuestions.questionText: Use ANNEXURE B (assembly instructions for pedal go-kart). Choose a picture from COLUMN B that matches the written instruction in COLUMN A. Write only the letter (A-E) next to question numbers 2.2.1 to 2.2.5.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answers:
2.2.1: C
2.2.2: E
2.2.3: D
2.2.4: B
2.2.5: A
Mark 1-5: 5A correct order (1 mark each)
subQuestions.topic: Maps, Plans and Other Representations - Assembly Instructions

subQuestions.questionText: The pictures (Picture 1: child on go-kart on flat ground; Picture 2: child on go-kart in long grass with a cross through it) illustrate safety instructions for using the pedal go-kart. Write down an explanation for ONE of the safety instructions illustrated in the pictures.
subQuestions.memoText:
Picture 1 example: Only use the go-cart on level ground / smooth, flat, hard, tarred road surface.
Picture 2 example: Do not use the vehicle on a long grassy surface / Do not drive off the road.
Mark 1-2: 2O explanation for 1st picture or for 2nd picture (2 marks)
subQuestions.topic: Maps, Plans and Other Representations - Safety Instructions

subQuestions.questionText: TABLE 2 shows the number of horses, small livestock and cattle from the Free State, Gauteng and other provinces on display at the Bloem Agricultural Show. One value (X) has been omitted (Gauteng small livestock). Free State: 612 horses, 1476 small livestock, 363 cattle, total 2451. Gauteng: 163 horses, X small livestock, 62 cattle, total 565. Other: 585 horses, 1024 small livestock, 371 cattle, total 1980. Totals: 1360 horses, 2840 small livestock, 796 cattle, 4996 grand total. Determine missing value X.
subQuestions.memoText:
$X = 2840 - 1476 - 1024 = 340$
OR $X = 565 - 163 - 62 = 340$
Mark 1: 1MA subtracting from total
Mark 2: 1CA simplification (340)
AO (answer only) - full marks

subQuestions.questionText: Write down, in simplified fractional form, the probability of NOT randomly selecting a horse from the total number of animals shown in TABLE 2 above.
subQuestions.memoText:
$P(\text{not a horse}) = \frac{2840 + 796}{4996} = \frac{3636}{4996} = \frac{909}{1249}$
Mark 1: 1RT numerator (3636 or values 2840 + 796)
Mark 2: 1RT denominator (4996)
Mark 3: 1A simplification ($\frac{909}{1249}$)
Alternative: $P(\text{horse}) = \frac{1360}{4996}$, $P(\text{not a horse}) = 1 - \frac{1360}{4996} = \frac{909}{1249}$
Mark 1: 1RT both values
Mark 2: 1MCA subtracting from 1
Mark 3: 1A simplification

subQuestions.questionText: A farmer visits the display where all the cattle are kept. He is specifically interested in purchasing cattle from the Free State. Calculate, as a percentage, the probability of the farmer randomly selecting cattle from the Free State.
subQuestions.memoText:
$P = \frac{363}{796} \times 100\% = 45,60301508\%$
Mark 1: 1RT 1st value (363)
Mark 2: 1RT 2nd value correctly placed (796)
Mark 3: 1CA simplification (≈ 45,6%)
NPR (no penalty for rounding)

questions.title: Wind Turbines, Compost Box, and Temperature Conversion

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the picture showing wind turbines and generation capacity from 1980 to 2005. Write down the amount of power generated by the wind turbine with the second-tallest hub height.
subQuestions.memoText:
2 000 kW
Mark 1-2: 2RT correct kW (2 marks)
NPU (no penalty for omitting units)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE possible reason why the rotor blade size of the wind turbine from 2005 is larger than the rotor blade size of the wind turbine from 1980.
subQuestions.memoText:
Possible answers:
- To allow rotor blade to produce more energy.
- Advanced technology to have material that can allow a big structure to stand firm on the ground.
- Larger rotor diameters allow wind turbines to sweep more area, capture more wind and produce more electricity.
- Demand for electricity increased / demand for cleaner electricity.
Mark 1-2: 2O reason (more electricity) (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate, in metres, the maximum height that the tip of the rotor blade of the tallest wind turbine can reach as it turns. (Tallest wind turbine: hub height 114 m, rotor diameter 124 m.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Max. height = Pole height + radius of rotor = $114 + \frac{124}{2} = 114 + 62 = 176$ m
Mark 1: 1RT both correct values (114 and 124)
Mark 2: 1MA divide by 2 to determine the radius
Mark 3: 1CA simplification (176 m)
Alternative: Pole + rotor = 124 + 114 = 238; Max height = 238 - (124÷2) = 238 - 62 = 176
AO (answer only) accepted.

subQuestions.questionText: Anam says that the area covered by the rotor blade of the tallest wind turbine in motion is 12 077,748 m². Verify, with calculations, whether or not her statement is VALID. (Use Area of a circle = 3,142 × radius².)
subQuestions.memoText:
Radius = $\frac{124}{2} = 62$ m
Area = $3,142 \times (62)^2 = 12\,077,848$ m²
Not valid (statement is INVALID).
Mark 1: 1A radius (62)
Mark 2: 1SF substitution squared
Mark 3: 1CA simplification (12 077,848)
Mark 4: 1O invalid
Note: Using 124 m as radius but correct calculation gives 48 311,392 m² and conclusion - award 2 out of 4.

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the percentage increase in power generation from 1995 to 2005. (1995: 800 kW; 2005: 5000 kW)
subQuestions.memoText:
% increase = $\frac{5000 - 800}{800} \times 100\% = 525\%$
Mark 1: 1RT 1st correct value (5000)
Mark 2: 1A denominator (800)
Mark 3: 1MA percentage
Mark 4: 1CA simplification (525%)
Alternative: Current % = $\frac{5000}{800} \times 100\% = 625\%$; % increase = 625% - 100% = 525%

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE other possible source of generating electricity that can be used in South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
Possible answers: Generators OR solar power OR hydro-power OR nuclear power. Also accept: water, coal, sun, inverters.
Mark 1-2: 2A source (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Use ANNEXURE C (rectangular compost box with sections A, B and C, with dimensions 2,3 m and 3 m). Calculate the perimeter of the base of the compost box. Use Perimeter of a rectangle = 2 × (length + width).
subQuestions.memoText:
Perimeter = $2 \times (2,3 + 2,3 + 2,3 + 3)$ m = $2 \times (6,9 + 3)$ m = 19,8 m
Mark 1: 1RT correct values
Mark 2: 1SF substitution
Mark 3: 1MA 6,9
Mark 4: 1CA answer (19,8 m)
Alternative: Perimeter = 3 + 2,3 + 2,3 + 2,3 + 3 + 2,3 + 2,3 + 2,3 m = 19,8 m

subQuestions.questionText: First, the boxes of Section A and Section C were completely assembled. The box in Section B fits in between Section A and Section C. Section B has fewer front panel boards than the back and shares side panel boards with Section A and Section C, as shown on ANNEXURE C. Determine how many additional panel boards are required to completely assemble the box in Section B.
subQuestions.memoText:
$5 + 7 + 4 = 16$ boards
Mark 1: 1RT correct numbers 5 and 7
Mark 2: 1A on 4
Mark 3: 1CA simplification adding (16)
AO (answer only) accepted.
Note: Answer of 12 - award 3 out of 3. Answer of 15 - award 2 out of 3.

subQuestions.questionText: The maximum height of the decomposing compost matter in each section, C : B : A, is in the ratio 3 : 5 : 7. Determine, in litres, the total capacity for the decomposing matter in Section A and Section B. (Use Volume = length × width × height; 1 m³ = 1 000 litres. Section A height = 0,5 m; sections are 2,3 m × 3 m.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Height B = $\frac{5}{7} \times 0,5$ m = 0,3571428571 m
Vol B = $2,3 \times 3 \times 0,3571428571 = 2,464285714$ m³
Vol A = $2,3 \times 3 \times 0,5 = 3,45$ m³
Total = $2,464285714 + 3,45 = 5,914285714$ m³
Capacity = $1000 \times 5,914285714 = 5\,914,285714$ litres
Mark 1: 1A height box B
Mark 2: 1CA volume of B box
Mark 3: 1SF volume of A box
Mark 4: 1A simplification 3,45
Mark 5: 1CA total volume
Mark 6: 1CA answer in litres
NPR

subQuestions.questionText: If the temperature rises above 70 °C, the compost will sterilise itself (kill the good micro-organisms). Convert this temperature to degrees Fahrenheit. Use the formula: $°C = \frac{5}{9} \times (°F - 32°)$
subQuestions.memoText:
$°C = \frac{5}{9} \times (°F - 32°)$
$70° = \frac{5}{9} \times (°F - 32°)$
$70° \times \frac{9}{5} = °F - 32$
$126° = °F - 32$
$°F = 158$
Mark 1: 1SF substituting in formula
Mark 2: 1MA changing subject
Mark 3: 1CA answer (158°F)
Note: Using formula $°F = (°C \times \frac{9}{5}) + 32$ correctly - no part marks - awarded 3 out of 3.

questions.title: School Layout Plan, Tiling, and Strip Map (Travel)

subQuestions.questionText: Use ANNEXURE D (school layout plan). Write down, in simplified form, the ratio of the number of single doors to the number of double doors on the school layout plan. (30 single doors and 6 double doors)
subQuestions.memoText:
$30 : 6 = 5 : 1$
Mark 1: 1RT 30
Mark 2: 1RT 6
Mark 3: 1A simplification (5 : 1)
subQuestions.topic: Maps, Plans and Other Representations - Ratio

subQuestions.questionText: Name the rooms that have TWO double doors and ONE single door.
subQuestions.memoText:
Reading room and computer lab
Mark 1-2: 2A 1st room
Mark 3: 1A second room

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE feature that indicates that the school has more than one level.
subQuestions.memoText:
Stairs
Mark 1-2: 2A stairs (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: During an evacuation drill, Anda took the following route: Exited the room and turned left into the hallway; Went straight past three single doors on the left and a fire extinguisher on the right; Turned right at the end of that hallway; Passed two rooms each having a double door; Then used the 'Exit to use in case of fire'. Determine the room from which Anda exited during the evacuation drill.
subQuestions.memoText:
Multi-media room 1
Mark 1-2: 2A correct room
Mark 3: 1A correct number
subQuestions.topic: Maps, Plans and Other Representations - Routes

subQuestions.questionText: The laboratory floor needs to be re-tiled. The dimensions of the tiles that will be used are: 600 mm × 600 mm. There are five tiles in a box. (The laboratory has an L-shape with dimensions: outer length 14 m, inner length 11 m, total width 7 m, with a 3,5 m × 3 m notch cut out.) The science teacher claimed that they would need a minimum of 40 boxes of tiles to tile the laboratory floor if cutting and breakages are ignored. Verify, showing ALL calculations, if his claim is VALID. Use the formula: Area of a rectangle = length × width.
subQuestions.memoText:
Area A = $11 \times 3,5 = 38,5$ m²
Area B = $14 \times 3,5 = 49$ m²
Floor area = $38,5 + 49 = 87,5$ m²
Area of tile = $600 \times 600 = 360\,000$ mm² = $0,36$ m²
Number of tiles = $\frac{87,5}{0,36} \approx 243,056$ tiles
Number of boxes = $\frac{244}{5} = 48,8 \approx 49$
INVALID (claim is not valid - need 49 boxes, not 40)
Mark 1: 1SF substitution
Mark 2: 1MCA simplification (38,5)
Mark 3: 1MA simplification (49)
Mark 4: 1MCA simplification total area (87,5)
Mark 5: 1A area tile (360 000 mm²)
Mark 6: 1C conversion (to 0,36 m²)
Mark 7: 1MCA dividing
Mark 8: 1CA number of tiles
Mark 9: 1CA number of boxes
Mark 10: 1O opinion (INVALID)
Alternative: Floor Area = 11×7 + 3,5×3 = 77 + 10,5 = 87,5 m². Tiles in 40 boxes = 40×5 = 200; 200 < 244, INVALID.

subQuestions.questionText: Use ANNEXURE E (strip map of roads connecting Zambia to South Africa). Write down the total number of countries shown on the strip map.
subQuestions.memoText:
4 (Zambia, Zimbabwe, South Africa, Botswana)
Mark 1-2: 2A number of countries (2 marks)
Note: Listing the four countries - award 1 out of 2.

subQuestions.questionText: Name the town that is 403 km from Bulawayo.
subQuestions.memoText:
Harare
Mark 1-2: 2A correct town (2 marks)

subQuestions.label: 4.2.3(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Anda travelled from Victoria Falls to Bulawayo. He had to pick up a friend from Hwange N.P. before reaching Bulawayo. Anda left Victoria Falls at 09:55 and travelled at an average speed of 97 km/h to Hwange N.P. (distance 179 km). Determine, to the nearest minute, at what time he reached his friend. You may use the formula: Speed = distance ÷ time.
subQuestions.memoText:
$97 = \frac{179}{\text{time}}$
Time = $\frac{179}{97} = 1,845$ hours
Time duration = 1 hour + $0,845 \times 60$ min = 1 hour 51 min
Arrival time = 09:55 + 1 h 51 min = 11:46
Mark 1: 1A 179
Mark 2: 1SF substitution 97
Mark 3: 1MCA change formula
Mark 4: 1CA time in hours
Mark 5: 1CA answer (11:46)
Accept 11:45.

subQuestions.label: 4.2.3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the total distance he travelled from Victoria Falls to Bulawayo. (Victoria Falls at 713 km mark, Bulawayo at 263 km mark, with detours of 18 km each way to pick up friend at Hwange N.P.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Distance = $(713 - 263) + 2(18) = 450 + 36 = 486$ km
Mark 1: 1MA subtracting correct values
Mark 2: 1MA getting 36
Mark 3: 1CA total distance (486 km)
Alternative: Distance = (713 - 552) + 18 + 18 + (552 - 263) = 161 + 18 + 18 + 289 = 486 km
Alternative: Distance = 179 + 18 + (552 - 263) = 486 km

questions.title: Apartment Building, Conversions, and Glass Panels Cost

subQuestions.questionText: Bontle owns a four-storey building with eight similar apartments, which she rents out. Use ANNEXURE F (layout plan of the ground floor showing two apartments). Write down the number of enclosed balconies in this building.
subQuestions.memoText:
8
Mark 1-2: 2A correct number (2 marks)
Note: Answer of 6 or 2 - award 1 out of 2.

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate, in feet, missing value A on the layout plan. (Total exterior length of the building is 58 feet; rooms are 11 feet wide with 2 feet wall thickness, with 4 such sections)
subQuestions.memoText:
Front entrance portal = $58 - (11 \times 4 + 2 \times 4) = 6$ feet
Mark 1: 1MA subtracting from 58
Mark 2: 1RT room dimensions
Mark 3: 1RT wall thickness
Mark 4: 1A multiplying with 4
Mark 5: 1CA simplification (6 feet)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE valid reason why Bontle stated that the apartments are open-plan living.
subQuestions.memoText:
There are no walls separating the kitchen, dining room and living room.
Mark 1-2: 2O reason (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the name of ONE common feature found in each of the bathrooms.
subQuestions.memoText:
Toilet OR bath OR basin or sink (also accept door)
Mark 1-2: 2A correct feature (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: One of the apartment entrance doors has 3B as a number. Give a possible interpretation of this number.
subQuestions.memoText:
Possible answers:
- 3rd floor and B that it is the second apartment
- Block B, Number 3
- 3rd Floor, unit on the left/right
- 3rd Floor, B-wing
Mark 1: 1O numbering of the floors
Mark 2: 1O numbering of the apartments

subQuestions.label: 5.1.6(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Bontle calculated the exterior length of the building to be 17,6784 m. Determine, rounded to THREE decimal places, the conversion factor she used in the form 1 m = ... feet.
subQuestions.memoText:
17,6784 m = 58 feet
Conversion factor: $1 \text{ m} = \frac{58}{17,6784} = 3,28083989... \approx 3,281$ feet
Mark 1: 1RT 58
Mark 2: 1MA simplification
Mark 3: 1R rounded answer (3,281 feet)

subQuestions.label: 5.1.6(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Hence, convert to metres the exterior width of the building. (Exterior width = 40 feet)
subQuestions.memoText:
Width = $\frac{40}{3,281} = 12,191405$ m
Mark 1: 1RT correct width (40)
Mark 2: 1MCA dividing
Mark 3: 1CA simplification (≈ 12,19 m)
CA from 5.1.6(a)
Alternative: 58 feet = 17,6784 m; 40 feet = n; $n = \frac{40}{58} \times 17,6784 = 12,191405$ m
NPR (no penalty for rounding)

subQuestions.questionText: The entrance door of the apartment building is a double door with six equally sized glass panels. Inner dimensions of one glass panel: 0,614 m × 0,474 m. Calculate, rounded to ONE decimal place, the area of ONE glass panel. Use Area of a rectangle = length × width.
subQuestions.memoText:
Area = $0,614 \times 0,474 = 0,291036$ m² ≈ 0,3 m²
Mark 1: 1SF substitution
Mark 2: 1R simplification (0,3 m²)
NPU (no penalty for omitting unit)

subQuestions.questionText: Bontle wants to replace all the glass panels with laminated safety glass. Information: Mass of safety glass = 15 kg per m²; Price = R490 per m²; Delivery charge = R820 for the first 20 kg, and thereafter R53,50 per kg or part thereof; Consider only inner measurements (ignore overlaps). Bontle stated that it will cost her less than R2 000 for the purchase and delivery of all the safety glass panels for the double door. Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether her statement is VALID.
subQuestions.memoText:
Area for 6 panels = $0,3 \times 6 = 1,8$ m²
Cost for 6 panels = $1,8 \times 490 = R882$
Mass of 6 panels = $1,8 \times 15 = 27$ kg
Delivery mass = 20 kg + 7 kg
Cost of delivery = $R820 + R53,50 \times 7 = R1\,194,50$
Total cost = $R882 + R1\,194,50 = R2\,076,50$
INVALID (statement is not valid - cost exceeds R2 000)
Mark 1: 1MCA simplification (1,8 m²)
Mark 2: 1MCA simplification cost (R882)
Mark 3: 1MCA simplification mass (27 kg)
Mark 4: 1MA cost of 1st 20 kg (R820)
Mark 5: 1MCA add and multiply
Mark 6: 1CA simplification (R1 194,50)
Mark 7: 1CA simplification (R2 076,50)
Mark 8: 1O verification (INVALID)
CA from Q 5.2.1
Alternative using unrounded area (0,291036): Area for 6 = 1,746216 m²; Cost = R855,65; Mass = 26,19324 kg ≈ 27 kg (round up); Total = R2 050,15; INVALID.
Note: Using rounded area 0,3 m² and rounding up to 2 m²: Cost = R980; Mass = 30 kg; Delivery = R820 + R53,50×10 = R1 355; Total = R2 335; INVALID - award 7 out of 8.
